Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
638 PM EST Sat Nov 14 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 153 PM EST Saturday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 153 PM EST Saturday...

1. Rain and snow showers will continue across the region this 
afternoon and evening, especially in the favored upslope locations. 
Showers will taper off through the day tomorrow. 

2. A warm, dry and mostly sunny week is in store.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 153 PM EST Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Cyclonic northwest flow will continue as the region 
remains under the influence of an upper level low this weekend. An 
embedded shortwave will pass through the region, bringing more 
widespread shower activity this afternoon into the evening. It's 
been a mix of rain and snow across the region today, with snow 
mostly confined to the high terrain and portions of the Northeast 
Kingdom this afternoon and rain most other locations. Although most 
locations are above freezing, temperatures may drop significantly 
within some of the showers, allowing for a rain/snow mix or even a 
brief period of snow at lower elevations. The widespread shower 
activity will end tonight, with lingering showers tapering off 
through the day tomorrow. Total snowfall accumulations this weekend 
look to generally be in the 1-4 inch range for locations above 2000 
ft, with little to no accumulation expected at lower elevations. 
Temperatures will continue to remain on the cooler side this 
weekend, with daytime highs only climbing into the 30s to lower 40s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Unimpactful weather is expected all of the way through 
the upcoming week into next weekend. Following one last seasonably 
cool day on Monday, temperatures should be near to around 10 degrees 
above normal for the remainder of the period. In fact, our large 
scale pattern strongly favors above normal temperatures to continue 
for much of the following week, as well. This week does not look 
particularly unseasonable, however. There is only a weak signal for 
unusually high daytime temperatures on Wednesday and Thursday, 
particularly in the Champlain and Lower Connecticut River valleys, 
ahead of a likely cold front. Said front is currently favored to 
track through with little fanfare Friday morning; eventually PoPs 
will probably increase when timing of this boundary becomes more 
clear; many ensemble and deterministic models show a period of some 
light precipitation associated with the feature. This will be the 
primary exception to a period of otherwise fair weather, with 
ridging re-establishing itself at the start of next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 00Z Monday...A mix of rain and snow showers continues to
shift south across the region. Intermittent precipitation will
continue through the next 4-8 hours, and then become
increasingly tied to terrain from 06z-12z and beyond. Ceilings 
range from 800-3000 ft agl, and little is expected to change, 
except some slight improvement at KMSS. Intervals of reduced 
visibility to 2-5 SM is possible in heavier showers, and may be 
closer to 1SM in snow showers. Slow improvement is expected past
13-15z under increasing northwest winds around 5-10 knots, but 
many terminals could remain MVFR over the next 24 hours.
